html:
Kava is a drink made from the root of a pepper plant, drunk across much of the Pacific for its calming effect. The plant was probably first domesticated in northern Vanuatu, which still grows the most varieties.

From there it spread east with voyagers to Fiji, Tonga, Samoa and Hawaii. In Fiji and western Polynesia, kava ceremonies are at the heart of chiefly rank, welcome and politics: who serves and who drinks first is laid down by custom.

Missionaries tried to ban it, with little success. In Vanuatu, nakamal kava bars are where men meet each evening, and kava is now a growing export, though several European countries banned it for some years after 2002.
